# Carlos Asmat

> Engineering leader who builds multi-disciplinary teams to turn ideas into world-class robotic and software products that ship at consumer scale. Carlos specializes in robotics, embedded systems, and connected devices.

Carlos Asmat is a robotics engineering leader whose work spans humanoid interaction robots, autonomous consumer robots, and wearable platforms. His career covers the full product lifecycle, from concept and prototype through architecture, team formation, and commercial deployment. His passion is building brilliant, cross-functional teams that can solve seemingly impossible problems and ship them to the real world.

At Aldebaran (later SoftBank Robotics) he wrote the physical and verbal interaction behaviors for the NAO and Pepper humanoid robots, including the demos for Neil deGrasse Tyson and Buzz Aldrin. He then helped take a robotics startup from idea to a shipped consumer product, leading early system architecture across electrical hardware, embedded software, and robotics, and growing the engineering teams that delivered it. That product paired an embedded vision neural network for user-following with a patented self-balancing two-wheel drive.

Today he leads architecture and system integration for embedded robotic platforms: setting technical strategy, rearchitecting controller systems for larger deployments, designing the telemetry and data infrastructure, growing the teams, and mentoring engineers across firmware, hardware, and software.

Across these roles the through-line has been technology strategy paired with the business growth that follows from shipping reliable systems at consumer scale, to audiences in the tens of thousands. He builds brilliant, multi-disciplinary teams that turn audacious ideas into real-world products and drives them to delivery.

## Site structure

- [Resume](https://asmat.ca/)
- [Blog](https://asmat.ca/blog/)
- [RSS Feed](https://asmat.ca/feed.xml)

## Featured posts

- [Bump it, Bro: Embrace the Limitations](https://asmat.ca/blog/bump-it-bro/) - Designing physical social interactions (fist bumps, hugs, handshakes) for NAO and Pepper robots at Aldebaran. Covers human-robot interaction design under hardware constraints, with demos for Neil deGrasse Tyson, Buzz Aldrin, Tyra Banks, and will.i.am.
- [The Wind Turbine, Part 2: Design and Materials](https://asmat.ca/blog/the-wind-turbine-part-2-desing-materials/) - Long-form build log for the IBee wind turbine: parts sourced from PVC pipe, a desktop case panel, and a salvaged AC motor, in preparation for an off-grid deployment in rural Ecuador.
- [Perfection?](https://asmat.ca/blog/perfection/) - Essay on the two meanings of "perfect" (the Latin sense of completion versus the modern sense of flawlessness) and why the flawlessness reading quietly breaks down outside closed conceptual systems.
- [Hold Me Tight](https://asmat.ca/blog/hold-me-tight/) - Custom engagement ring designed with 3D scanning, jewelry CAD, and lost-wax casting.

## Areas of expertise

- Technology strategy and business growth for consumer products at scale
- Multi-disciplinary team building (EE, firmware, software, robotics) and driving teams to delivery
- Reliable software systems for audiences in the tens of thousands
- Robotics engineering leadership, full product lifecycle
- Human-robot interaction (HRI), social robotics, interaction design
- Humanoid robots, autonomous consumer robots, exoskeletons
- Embedded systems, embedded vision, neural networks on device
- System architecture, controller design, telemetry infrastructure
- Electronics, Arduino, FPGA
- Linux, C++/Python, ROS

## Blog

The blog has two sections:

- **Recent posts** (2019+): Current writing on software, robotics, and tools
- **Carlitos' Contraptions Archive** (2006-2013): Restored from the old carlitoscontraptions.com blog, covering personal maker projects, robotics (including the Nao 1337 humanoid robot), electronics, Arduino, and DIY builds
